h1: The 4 Best 40V Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four Greenworks 40V cordless leaf blowers, from 135 CFM sweepers to a 730 CFM yard clearer, with picks by yard size.
summary: The 730 CFM Greenworks 40V is the best of the four, the strongest airflow and the only pick built for heavy, wet leaves. The 550 CFM model is the sensible buy for an average lot, and the 500 CFM version is nearly the same at the same tier. The 135 CFM unit is a light-duty sweeper for patios and decks.
intro: The 40V badge on a leaf blower is about the battery, not the wind. It tells you which pack clicks into the tool and which other machines will share it, and says nothing about how much air the blower moves. Within the same 40V family, the airflow gap between models can be more than fivefold, from 135 CFM up to 730, so the voltage is the least useful number on the box.

This ranking looks only at Greenworks 40V blowers whose listings name both the platform and an airflow figure. Others that did not confirm 40V were left out. We ranked on CFM first, then asked which yard each size really fits. Price tier follows airflow, but unevenly, so the order is not simply strongest to weakest.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Electric Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The strongest 40V airflow in this group at 730 CFM.
products.description:
The 730 CFM Greenworks is the one that actually shifts wet, matted leaf cover. It is a cordless blower on the 40V battery platform, rated at the highest airflow of the four, in the $200 to $500 bucket. CFM is volume per minute, and volume is what lifts heavy leaves instead of skating over them.

It ranks first because airflow decides how much a blower can clear, and nothing here comes close. Against the 550 CFM model, the cost is a full price tier for roughly a third more wind.

Choose it for a large yard with heavy leaf fall, where the extra volume saves time every autumn. The caveat is size and money: it is overkill for a small lawn, where a cheaper blower does the same job, and it is the most expensive of the group. Check whether a battery is included.
products.idealFor: Large yards with heavy leaf fall.
products.skipIf: You only clear a patio or small lawn.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Electric Leaf Blower (550 CFM)
products.verdict: A balanced 550 CFM blower for an average suburban lot.
products.description:
The 550 CFM Greenworks is the blower that suits most lots. It runs cordless on the 40V platform with 550 CFM, in the $100 to $200 bucket. For an ordinary yard with a few trees, that much airflow clears dry and lightly damp leaves in one or two passes.

It takes second because it delivers most of the top pick's airflow at roughly half the price tier. The gap is real only on stubborn wet leaves, where the 730 CFM model pulls ahead.

Buy it for a typical suburban property. The caveat is conditions: it is the middle of the range, so if your yard sees heavy, damp leaf cover each autumn, step up to the 730 CFM. For lighter work, it matches the 500 CFM version at the same tier and gives more air.
products.skipIf: You face heavy, wet leaf cover.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Cordless Leaf Blower (500 CFM)
products.verdict: Just under the 550 CFM model, at the same price tier.
products.description:
The 500 CFM Greenworks is the near-twin of the 550. It is a cordless 40V blower rated at 500 CFM, in the same $100 to $200 range. For a small or mid-size lawn, 500 CFM is enough to move dry leaves and clippings to the edge.

It ranks third because it offers 50 CFM less than the model above in the same tier. The gap is small, about nine percent, so it makes sense mainly when it is cheaper on the day you buy.

Choose it for small to mid-size lawns where price decides. The caveat is plain: if the 550 CFM version costs the same, take that one, since there is no clear edge here. Check that a battery and charger are included before comparing prices, because a bare tool changes the math.
products.skipIf: The 550 CFM model costs the same.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Cordless Leaf Blower (135 CFM)
products.verdict: A light-duty 135 CFM sweeper for patios and driveways.
products.description:
The 135 CFM Greenworks is a different kind of tool. It is a cordless 40V model rated at only 135 CFM, in the $100 to $200 bucket. At that airflow it works as a sweeper, pushing dust, grit and a few dry leaves off a patio, deck or driveway.

It comes last because its airflow is a fraction of the others, which limits it to light debris, and it costs a similar tier to stronger models. A 135 CFM stream cannot lift a damp, packed leaf layer.

Buy it for hard surfaces and tidy-up jobs. The caveat is the price comparison: at the same tier, the 500 or 550 CFM models do far more, so choose this only if you want a light, small tool for decks and walkways. Skip it for any real lawn clearing.
products.skipIf: You need to clear a lawn of leaves.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is the volume of air a blower moves each minute, and it matters because higher volume shifts wet and heavy leaves. Find the CFM number in the listing title or bullets, not just the word powerful. Here it runs from 135 to 730, and the difference is what you notice on the lawn when leaves are wet.

A 40V label means the blower uses a battery of that voltage, and matching packs can be shared with other tools on the platform. It does not measure airflow. Check the listing states 40V and whether the battery and charger are included, since a bare tool needs a separate purchase and the battery is the costly part.

A cordless blower removes the extension lead and lets you reach far corners. The tradeoff is a limited run time, which depends on the battery. Look for a power type line saying cordless, and consider a spare pack if your yard is large or leaf fall is heavy, because a single pack may not finish the job.

A bigger yard needs more airflow and more run time, while small patios do not. Compare the CFM against the area you clear, and size up if you have heavy leaf fall or wet leaves. A blower that is too weak just means more passes and a longer afternoon, plus more battery used for the same area.

Price rises with airflow, but not evenly: the 550 and 500 CFM models share a tier, and the 135 CFM unit costs the same tier as both. Compare each bucket against the CFM figure to see where the extra money goes, and avoid paying for less air at the same price, which is the common trap here.

faq.a: Not directly. Voltage defines the battery platform, while CFM measures airflow. Compare the CFM number between models, such as 730 against 550, and ignore the voltage for power, since all four are 40V.

Check each listing. Some bundles include the battery and charger, and bare tools do not, which changes the true cost, since a pack and charger add real money. Confirm that before you compare prices on the Greenworks models.

faq.q: Is the 730 CFM Greenworks worth it over the 550 CFM?
faq.a: Only for large yards or wet leaves. Most average lawns are handled by 550 CFM in a lower price tier, and the 730 CFM costs a full tier more, which only pays off with big, wet piles.

faq.q: How do I get the most from a cordless blower?
faq.a: Work with the wind and sweep leaves into piles in one direction. Fully charge the battery before a large job, and carry a spare pack if the yard is large, since runtime depends on the battery.
Clear debris from the intake and nozzle after use, and store the battery indoors away from extreme heat or cold. Wipe the housing so grit does not wear the switch, and check the nozzle for cracks.

faq.q: Is the 135 CFM model enough for a lawn?
faq.a: It is too weak for most lawn clearing. Keep the 135 CFM Greenworks for patios, decks and walkways, and choose a 500 or 550 CFM model for leaves on grass, where airflow does the work.

finalTake: Buy the 730 CFM Greenworks for a large yard with heavy leaf fall, or the 550 CFM model for an ordinary suburban lot. Take the 500 CFM only if it undercuts the 550 on the day, and keep the 135 CFM for patios, decks and walkways.
